'''Jay Fineberg''' ({{Langx|he|ג'יי פינברג}}; born 1956) is an Israeli physicist. He is a professor at [[The Racah Institute of Physics]] of the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Jay Fineberg |url=https://phys.huji.ac.il/contacts/fineberg_jay |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=phys.huji.ac.il |language=en}}</ref> He is known for his work on various aspects of nonlinear physics, mainly in the fields of [[fracture]] ('how things break') and [[friction]] ('how things slide').<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Home |url=http://old.phys.huji.ac.il/~jay/ |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=old.phys.huji.ac.il}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jay Fineberg |url=https://scholar.google.co.il/citations?user=gFWeBiUAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=scholar.google.co.il}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the Israel Physical Society.

== Education and career ==
Fineberg studied mathematics and physics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], graduating with Bachelor's degrees in both subjects in 1981. He later went on to earn his M.S. (1983) and Ph.D. (1988) in physics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Fineberg |first1=Jay |last2=Steinberg |first2=Victor |date=1987-03-30 |title=Vortex-front propagation in Rayleigh-Bénard convection |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=58 |issue=13 |pages=1332–1335 |doi=10.1103/physrevlett.58.1332 |pmid=10034404 |bibcode=1987PhRvL..58.1332F |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> He then moved to the center for nonlinear dynamics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] as a postdoc, where he started his career in the non-linear physics about fracture and friction.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last1=Livne |first1=Ariel |last2=Bouchbinder |first2=Eran |last3=Svetlizky |first3=Ilya |last4=Fineberg |first4=Jay |date=2010-03-12 |title=The Near-Tip Fields of Fast Cracks |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1180476 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=327 |issue=5971 |pages=1359–1363 |doi=10.1126/science.1180476 |pmid=20223982 |bibcode=2010Sci...327.1359L |s2cid=206522905 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" />

Fineberg joined [[the Racah Institute of Physics]] of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1992 and was appointed as a full professor in 2001.<ref name=":2" /> Fineberg served as the head of the Racah Institute of Physics (2005-2009), and as the Vice-Dean (2009-2011) and Dean (2016-2020) of the Faculty of Mathematics and Sciences.<ref name=":2" />

== Research ==
Fineberg's research interests have been mainly focused on the physics of fracture and friction.<ref name=":3" /> His early work includes the study of experimental nonlinear dynamics and nonlinear pattern-forming systems.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Arbell |first=H. |last2=Fineberg |first2=J. |date=2000-07-24 |title=Temporally Harmonic Oscillons in Newtonian Fluids |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.756 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=85 |issue=4 |pages=756–759 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.756 |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He discovered the localized micro-branching instabilities<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal |last1=Fineberg |first1=J. |last2=Marder |first2=M. |date=1999-05-01 |title=Instability in dynamic fracture |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370157398000854 |journal=Physics Reports |language=en |volume=313 |issue=1 |pages=1–108 |doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(98)00085-4 |bibcode=1999PhR...313....1F |issn=0370-1573|url-access=subscription }}</ref> during the fast crack propagation and validated the nonlinear propagating [[Solitary wave (water waves)|solitary wave]]<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last1=Sharon |first1=Eran |last2=Cohen |first2=Gil |last3=Fineberg |first3=Jay |date=2001 |title=Propagating solitary waves along a rapidly moving crack front |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35065051 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=410 |issue=6824 |pages=68–71 |doi=10.1038/35065051 |pmid=11242041 |bibcode=2001Natur.410...68S |s2cid=4357114 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> in the high-speed fracture process. Other interests include dynamics of crack propagation, crack tip singularity and crack fragmentation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kolvin |first1=Itamar |last2=Cohen |first2=Gil |last3=Fineberg |first3=Jay |date=2017-10-16 |title=Topological defects govern crack front motion and facet formation on broken surfaces |journal=Nature Materials |volume=17 |issue=2 |pages=140–144 |doi=10.1038/nmat5008 |pmid=29035358 |arxiv=1708.01881 |issn=1476-1122}}</ref><ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ben-David |first1=Oded |last2=Rubinstein |first2=Shmuel M. |last3=Fineberg |first3=Jay |date=January 2010 |title=Slip-stick and the evolution of frictional strength |journal=Nature |volume=463 |issue=7277 |pages=76–79 |doi=10.1038/nature08676 |pmid=20054393 |bibcode=2010Natur.463...76B |s2cid=4309635 |issn=0028-0836}}</ref>

Fineberg developed systematic experimental methods to study shear cracks, including real-time and high spatial observation of interfacial friction and laboratory [[earthquake]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal Condensed Matter Physics |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=253–273 |doi=10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031218-013327 |bibcode=2019ARCMP..10..253S |s2cid=125774756 |issn=1947-5454}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal == Awards and honors ==
In 2011 Fineberg was elected a fellow of the American Physical Society, cited for "his clever experiments and analyses of the dynamics of nonequilibrium systems, particularly concerning the propagation and instabilities of cracks in solids and gels, the dynamics of friction and earthquakes, and instabilities in oscillated liquid layers."<ref name="APS">{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2011&unit_id=GSNP |access-date=2022-11-19 |publisher=American Physical Society }}</ref> In 2021 he was elected a fellow of the Israel Physical Society for "his original and incisive contributions to the dynamics and instabilities of fractures, and the onset of dynamical friction."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=IPS Fellows - Israel Physical Society |url=https://www.israelphysicalsociety.org/ips-conference-2021/ips-fellows |access-date=2022-05-29 |publisher=Israel Physical Society |archive-date=2022-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813151259/https://www.israelphysicalsociety.org/ips-conference-2021/ips-fellows |url-status=dead }}</ref>
